background_notes.fact: For the D003 Fourier norms, if r<=s and f belongs to H^s, then f belongs to H^r and ||f||_{H^r}<=||f||_{H^s}. In particular L2 embeds in H^(-23/14), and H^gamma embeds in L2 when gamma>0.

grounds.reason: The Sobolev norms are weighted square sums with <k>>=1.
The X inputs have bounded L2 norms.

background_notes.justification: For every integer k, <k>^(2r)<=<k>^(2s). Sum the termwise nonnegative inequalities and take square roots; completion gives the inclusion of the spaces. Applying the same inequality at almost every time gives the corresponding L-infinity bound.

background_notes.fact: For 0<tau<=1 and real theta>=gamma, tau^theta<=tau^gamma; hence a bound uniform in t of the form K tau^theta ||w||_{H^gamma}^2 gives sup_t||F_n(t;w)||<=K M^2 tau^gamma when ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M.

w is the arbitrary mean-zero H^gamma input.
M is its retained H^gamma norm bound.
The numerical exponent comparisons theta>=gamma are explicitly proved here; admissibility is not supplied by these comparisons.

background_notes.justification: tau^theta=tau^gamma tau^(theta-gamma), and 0<tau^(theta-gamma)<=1 (equivalently use log tau<=0). The norm antecedent implies M>=0 and ||w||^2<=M^2; a uniform upper bound remains an upper bound on the supremum. This fact does not establish admissibility of any external loss.
